summary:
Fireline is a web app that merges NASA's MODIS (2000 onward) and VIIRS (2012 onward) FIRMS hotspots into one consistent monthly fire record. Pick any area by drawing it, searching a place or choosing a preset, and Fireline shows how much it burned each month since November 2000, whether the latest month is abnormal against the 2003-2022 median, and lets you download the numbers as CSV or ask questions in plain English.

VIIRS detects several times more hotspots than MODIS for the same fires, so the two records can't be joined directly. We count fire cell-days on a common H3 grid, calibrate VIIRS to MODIS per region and month over 2012-2019 with bootstrap error bands, and splice the series in 2020. This cuts the VIIRS/MODIS bias from 2.2-4.4x to about 1.1x, and an independent ESA Sentinel-3 check agrees (r = 0.87).

It matters now: Terra and Aqua MODIS end in 2027. Fireline keeps the 26-year fire record going on VIIRS, in MODIS-equivalent units.
details:
Fireline answers one question for any area: how much has it burned each month since 2000, on one consistent scale, and is this month unusual?

Slides: https://storage.googleapis.com/fireline-space-apps-data/public/demo/fireline-demo.pdf

WHAT IT DOES

- Pick an area: draw a polygon, enter a point and radius, search a place, or click a preset (Brazilian Pantanal, Western Canada, Indian Punjab).

- Burning calendar: one row per year, one column per month, switchable between counts and anomalies. Each cell shows the harmonized value with its 90% band, the 2003-2022 median, a robust z-score, percentile rank, and raw MODIS and VIIRS counts. An accessible table view carries the same numbers.

- Summary cards in plain sentences: this month vs normal, worst months and years, and a trend only when the data supports one.

- A sensor seam chart showing raw MODIS, raw VIIRS and the harmonized line together.

- CSV downloads of the monthly statistics and every cleaned hotspot in the area.

- A method page with validation results per region.

- An AI analyst that answers questions using tool calls over the same data, with a "How I got this" list of every call.

- An MCP server so AI assistants can query the fire history directly.

- A hexagon map of fire locations per month, and weather context (temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation anomalies) for presets.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: NASA FIRMS MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m hotspots (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21), standard files for the archive and near-real-time for recent months.

2. Cleaning: vegetation fires only, MODIS confidence >= 30, VIIRS nominal/high, dated by local solar day.

3. Common unit: a fire cell-day is one H3 res-8 cell (~0.74 km², about one MODIS pixel) with a detection from one satellite on one local day, so VIIRS's smaller pixels no longer inflate counts. VIIRS is the mean over satellites flying that day, so a new satellite adds no fire.

4. Calibration: k = MODIS / VIIRS cell-days per region and calendar month over 2012-2019, shrunk toward the regional k for thin months, with 90% bands from a 1,000-draw year bootstrap.

5. Splice: observed MODIS through 2019, k x VIIRS from January 2020. The record continues after MODIS ends with no code change.

6. Validation: overlap bias drops from 2.18x / 2.98x / 4.44x (Pantanal / W Canada / Punjab) to 1.06x / 1.18x / 1.14x. Leave-one-year-out r = 0.98 / 0.98 / 0.97; forward test 2020-2025 r = 0.99 / 0.99 / 0.98. Independent check against ESA Sentinel-3: Spearman r = 0.866 over 64 months.

BENEFITS

Fire agencies and researchers can compare 2024 with 2005 without caring which satellite saw the fire. Every number has an error band, and the record carries on after Terra and Aqua MODIS end in 2027.

LIMITATIONS

Different overpass times, Terra/Aqua orbit drift since ~2020, provisional near-real-time months, noisy small areas, and a 2020 seam test that can't separate sensor artifacts from real change. The method page covers each.

TOOLS

Python (DuckDB with spatial and H3, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, matplotlib) for the pipeline; TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Google Maps Platform, Terra Draw, deck.gl, Observable Plot, h3-js and Zod for the app; Gemini on Vertex AI via the Vercel AI SDK; MCP TypeScript SDK; Google Cloud Run and Cloud Storage; Docker.

Source code: https://github.com/atontalapur/fireline

Open data (no login): https://storage.googleapis.com/fireline-space-apps-data/public/v1/index.json
